title: Normalized support localization for a monomorphism on a site
statement: Let C be a small category in the stated common universes, J a Grothendieck topology on C, A a commutative ring, and j:W→V a monomorphism. For ordinary sheaves of A-modules, let supported sections be the kernel of restriction from V to W [def-pur-support-cohomology]. There exist natural connecting morphisms δ^q for every integer q on the entire bounded-below derived category, forming the three exactness assertions of SupportSequenceExact [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. They satisfy supportBoundaryNormalization [def-pur-support-comparison-boundary-maps]: on every bounded-below termwise injective complex, the restriction row is short exact and δ is exactly its snake boundary under the canonical right-derived-unit homology comparisons. No finite-coefficient or scheme hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 09XP, label section-cohomology-support, injective kernel/restriction sequence; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 093X, label lemma-restriction-along-monomorphism-surjective; homology.tex Tag 0117, label lemma-long-exact-sequence-cochain.

proof.text: Restriction along j is surjective on any injective module sheaf M. The free module presheaf on the representable W maps monomorphically into that on V: at each object its basis map is injective because j is mono. Sheafification preserves this monomorphism. A section over W defines a map from the sheafified free module on W into M; extend it along the monomorphism using injectivity and evaluate the resulting map at the generator over V. Naturality gives a section over V restricting to the original one. This proof uses the actual free-module Yoneda maps and generators in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Sites.InjectiveSheafSmulEpi, and makes the extension and evaluation explicit.

The supported-sections inclusion and restriction are natural transformations whose composite vanishes by the kernel condition. On injective objects the resulting row is short exact, since its first arrow is the kernel inclusion and its second arrow is surjective by Step 1. Apply the normalized derived connecting-map theorem to these three additive functors. Whisker the resulting natural transformations with the full subcategory for the top object property. Its normalization at QI with identity model is exactly supportBoundaryNormalization.

Represent each bounded-below derived coefficient by a bounded-below complex of injectives, using the injective homotopy-category equivalence. The three exactness assertions of the short exact homology sequence, transported through the canonical derived-unit model isomorphisms, are SupportSequenceExact. This is injectiveBoundary_exact from the normalized derived-boundary API.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_site_normalized_support_sequence
    {C : Type (u + 1)} [Category.{u} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A]
    {V W : C} (j : W ⟶ V) [Mono j] :
    ∃ δ : Sheaf.SupportSequenceBoundary J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j ⊤,
      supportBoundaryNormalization J A j δ ∧
        Sheaf.SupportSequenceExact J (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j ⊤ δ
